description: Schema and semantic vectors for one stable Direct Conversation per pair: the caller-authored four-Event founding unit with explicit peer and founder membership and its self/peer carrier branches, first-valid-unit slot admission across same-server, dual-server and multi-device concurrency, suspend/rejoin, MLS-generation separation, participant authority and root masking, plus the Contact list next_prepare_input successor cursor and the pending_incoming request_receipt that author the respond, reject, scope_update and tombstone prepare phases the same Contact lineage feeds, the sixteen-candidate active-generation fanout cap, and the server-verifiable narrowing of the resolver send blocker set.

schema_validation_cases.name: founding_authority_evidence_rejects_mixed_branches
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: contains:is not valid under any of the given schemas

schema_validation_cases.name: legacy_flat_found_outcome_rejected
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: contains:not valid under any of the given schemas

semantic_cases.name: existing_offline_agent_is_found
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding exists; agent presence offline and KeyPackage inventory is zero
semantic_cases.action: resolve
assertions: state is found
same Realm and main Strand are returned
no KeyPackage claim occurs
the query-only resolver performs no create phase

semantic_cases.name: repair_dispatch_is_a_non_authorizing_durable_trigger
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair has an accepted binding, one participant has an accepted ak.member.rejoin.own, the MLS group needs a replacement generation, and the peer participant is offline
semantic_cases.action: submit one exact device-or-Native-Agent authorized request through ak.self.direct_conversation.command.repair_dispatch and let the source relay it through ak.peer.direct_conversation.command.repair_relay
assertions: the self request and peer relay use their registered closed operation DTOs; only the destination's internal human-device branch creates DeviceMessageEnvelope values, while a Native Agent branch targets its accepted current runtime endpoint without inventing an ak:device id
the request is not carried on the Signal rail, whose 120 second live envelope cannot reach an offline peer

the request carries no Event bytes, no MLS material and no authority: the peer re-verifies requester identity, the accepted rejoin, both directional Contact heads and generation staleness from the signed event log before authoring anything
the resolver supplies active_mls_generation_ref and sha256(RFC8785_JCS(current accepted active-generation cell whole value)) as one pair in found and in every repairable suspended state
the request copies observed_active_generation_value_digest byte for byte from that resolver value and never hashes the Event ref or scans for a maximum generation
a request whose observed_active_generation_value_digest differs from the peer current whole-value digest is dropped instead of producing a second replacement generation
the source transaction freezes request digest, current destination binding, exact relay bytes and outbox before network delivery; retry and restart never rebuild from newer state

the destination transaction chooses exactly one recipient_target branch: human_principal atomically fans identical canonical content to every current-authorized-device snapshot with distinct stable message ids, or native_agent atomically targets the one current active accepted runtime endpoint

the exact KeyPackage claim uses one closed target selector: a human has exactly one target_device_ids entry; an Agent has target_agent_id, target_agent_verification_method and target_agent_key_authorize_event_id and forbids target_device_ids; both consume exactly requester_keypackage_ref
there is no ack, receipt or refusal code: the durable Commit, Welcome and activation are the only response, and refusal is simply a generation that never advances
concurrent repairers are resolved by the existing candidate fanout cap and security_barrier CAS, with no repair-specific winner rule

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_destination_atomic_replay
semantic_cases.precondition: one destination accepted the first relay under (Source-Service-ID, request_id) and persisted its terminal outcome
semantic_cases.action: redeliver the exact canonical relay body, then reuse request_id with one changed content byte
assertions: the exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome without resnapshotting targets or allocating another message id
the changed digest returns duplicate_conflict and writes zero queue entries
a crash before the atomic commit leaves neither the request ledger nor any target queue item; a crash after commit exposes the complete original batch and outcome

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_human_recipient_snapshot_is_all_or_zero
semantic_cases.precondition: the accepted peer participant is human with three current authorized devices and the third queue write fails
semantic_cases.action: process the peer repair relay
assertions: recipient_target.kind is human_principal
zero messages and zero terminal ledger outcome are committed
a retry may take one new authoritative snapshot only because no first transaction committed; once committed, later device authorization or revocation never mutates the frozen snapshot

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_native_agent_uses_runtime_not_device
semantic_cases.precondition: the accepted peer participant is a Native Agent with one current active runtime endpoint in accepted Agent key/session binding
semantic_cases.action: process the peer repair relay
assertions: recipient_target.kind is native_agent and enqueued_target_count is exactly one
the target snapshot transcript binds recipient_agent_id, active_runtime_endpoint_ref and stable device_message_id
no ak:device id, device projection or per-device queue is synthesized
missing, ambiguous, stale or inactive runtime binding fails closed with zero enqueue

semantic_cases.name: repair_exact_keypackage_target_xor
semantic_cases.precondition: claim_purpose is direct_conversation_repair
semantic_cases.action: attempt human, Native Agent, mixed and stale exact selectors
assertions: human accepts only target_keypackage_ref plus exactly one target_device_ids and returns exactly that ref with matching device evidence

Native Agent accepts only target_keypackage_ref plus target_agent_id, target_agent_verification_method and target_agent_key_authorize_event_id and returns exactly that ref with matching AgentSignerEvidence
mixed human and Agent selectors, absent exact ref, another current package, last-resort, consumed, revoked, wrong signer or stale authority all return opaque claim_failed with zero consumption

semantic_cases.name: creation_required_carries_the_authoring_material
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair has an accepted Contact round and no accepted Direct Conversation Realm; the caller is the founder and the current gates allow creation
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair through ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve
assertions: state is creation_required and next_founding_input is present

next_founding_input member names equal the DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission members byte for byte, so the caller copies founding_authority_evidence and origin Principal Server identity from the signed Events across with no renaming map
exactly one founding_authority_evidence branch is returned for this pair, human for a peer Contact founding and controller_agent for an own-Agent founding
the container carries no Event bytes, no coordinates, no idempotency_key and no receipt: the founder still authors and signs all four Events
a service that cannot assemble or verify the material returns temporarily_unavailable instead of a creation_required outcome without the container
the submission re-verifies the material against the service's own current state and never trusts the echoed copy

semantic_cases.name: accepted_service_binding_has_a_non_circular_producer
semantic_cases.precondition: the founder DID and PCR are accepted and the authenticated principal has no current service binding
semantic_cases.action: prepare a frozen binding draft, sign its challenge-bound digest, commit it, then resolve a creation-required pair
assertions: binding establishment runs after DID publication so the service derives current authority_evidence without a future-value dependency
prepare accepts no caller-supplied service metadata, DID evidence, timestamps, challenge or binding core
authorization_challenge equals challenge_id and is inside binding_digest, so an old principal proof cannot complete a fresh challenge
principal proof and service proof use distinct proof_purpose values and created_at equals the frozen accepted_at
current-binding CAS, immutable accepted binding, challenge consumption, service proof and byte-identical replay outcome commit atomically
same-service renewal requires predecessor_binding_digest to equal the complete current binding digest; a CAS loser writes nothing
resolver returns the durable verified binding verbatim, while no binding or unverifiable authority yields temporarily_unavailable

semantic_cases.name: same_founder_authority_recovery_is_not_succession
semantic_cases.precondition: the derived founder temporarily lost all usable devices, then ordinary account/device recovery restored control of the exact same (principal_id, principal_server_id) before any Direct Conversation Realm was accepted
semantic_cases.action: resolve and submit the original pair's founding unit with current ordinary founder authority evidence
assertions: the resolver may return creation_required only after the same exact authority pair again satisfies the ordinary current proof
the author is still the original derived founder and no succession Event, recovery generation, successor slot or additional authority source exists
pair_key and founding slot identity are unchanged

semantic_cases.name: founder_loss_never_transfers_the_same_pair_slot
semantic_cases.precondition: no accepted Direct Conversation Realm exists and the exact derived founder authority pair cannot currently be verified
semantic_cases.action: the non-founder attempts creation after a timeout, with a root Contact recovery policy, a third-party attestation, or an after-the-fact bilateral successor signature
assertions: zero Events, slots, receipts and coordinates are written
the non-founder resolver remains awaiting_founder regardless of elapsed time
the closed resolver union contains no founder_unrecoverable state and no local permanence inference becomes a consensus fact
the submission and Contact schemas contain no Direct Conversation founder successor, recovery authority or recovery generation field

semantic_cases.name: different_stable_identity_creates_a_new_non_continuous_pair
semantic_cases.precondition: one person adopts a genuinely new stable principal identity and establishes a new Contact with the peer because the old founder identity is unrecoverable
semantic_cases.action: derive and create a Direct Conversation for the new stable participant pair
assertions: the new stable participant tuple naturally derives a different pair_key without salt, generation or a versioned successor coordinate
the new Contact and Direct Conversation do not inherit old history, MLS state, keys, audit identity, founding receipt or authority
a product may show the old local transcript read-only but must label the cryptographic lineage as distinct

semantic_cases.name: founding_coordinates_are_derived_from_unit_bytes
semantic_cases.precondition: founder authored the four-Event unit in fixed wire order, ending with its explicit head_eq-null membership join
semantic_cases.action: submit the direct_conversation_founding branch of ak.self.events.command.submit
assertions: realm_id equals retype of the first Event ID and main_strand_id equals retype of the third Event ID
founding_unit_digest is recomputed from the four ordered Event IDs under the ak.direct-conversation.founding-unit.v1 domain
two independent implementations derive the same coordinates, unit digest and receipt semantics
acceptance fixes the caller-derived coordinates and allocates nothing

semantic_cases.name: founding_unit_strand_uses_bootstrap_no_basis_shape
semantic_cases.precondition: the third Event of the founding unit is the Realm's main ak.strand.create and the Genesis Seal covers all four Events
semantic_cases.action: admit the unit
assertions: the Strand carries neither seal_ref, auth_context nor seal_basis and rides the same-batch staged authority-root proof
a no-basis ak.strand.create outside this exact unit is rejected by batch admission
the same Strand carrying seal_ref, auth_context or seal_basis inside the unit is rejected

semantic_cases.name: server_allocated_founding_identifier_rejected
semantic_cases.precondition: a submission asserts a service-allocated realm_id, a reservation handle or a materialization draft
semantic_cases.action: submit the founding unit
assertions: zero Events are written
no coordinator election, reserved state or materializing state exists in the contract

semantic_cases.name: founder_multi_device_concurrency_admits_first_valid_unit
semantic_cases.precondition: two founder devices independently author different valid units for the same pair
semantic_cases.action: both submit concurrently to the same Principal Server slot
assertions: exactly one unit is accepted and four Events are written once
the losing device receives direct_conversation_slot_already_committed with zero writes
both devices then resolve to the same coordinates

semantic_cases.name: exact_unit_replay_returns_byte_identical_receipt
semantic_cases.precondition: the unit was accepted but the response was lost, or the service restarted after receipt persistence or outbox enqueue
semantic_cases.action: replay the same signed bytes with the same idempotency_key
assertions: the stored receipt is returned byte-identically and accepted_at does not advance
no second Event, receipt, slot or outbox entry is produced

semantic_cases.name: same_idempotency_key_different_unit_conflicts
semantic_cases.precondition: the caller reuses one idempotency_key with a different founding_unit_digest
semantic_cases.action: submit the second unit
assertions: zero Events are written

semantic_cases.name: same_and_dual_principal_server_deployments_agree
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair is hosted on one Principal Server in one run and on two Principal Servers in another
semantic_cases.action: run self founding and the federation direct_conversation_founding branch
assertions: both deployments produce the same unit digest, coordinates and admission decision
the federation branch omits service_binding_ref and binds destination through service DID headers and the source receipt

semantic_cases.name: federation_founding_dependency_missing_is_atomic
semantic_cases.precondition: the Contact round mirror has not reached the destination Principal Server
semantic_cases.action: deliver the founding unit through the peer direct_conversation_founding branch
assertions: the response is a top-level HTTP 409 with EventsDependencyMissingProblem
zero Events are written and no per-item partial acceptance occurs
the delivery remains retryable and is never permanently rejected

semantic_cases.name: leave_or_directional_contact_terminal_suspends
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding exists and leave, block, or either directional Contact head/scope gate becomes false; Consent is not consulted
semantic_cases.action: resolve and attempt message
assertions: resolver returns suspended with same coordinates
reason classes are not disclosed
no successor Realm is created

semantic_cases.name: rejoin_uses_same_realm_without_old_keys
semantic_cases.precondition: suspension basis is repaired
semantic_cases.action: resolve and rejoin
assertions: same binding Realm and main Strand are used
new active MLS generation is projected
old epoch keys and history secret are not automatically delivered

semantic_cases.name: generic_navigation_excludes_dm
semantic_cases.precondition: stable DM Realm is synchronized
semantic_cases.action: generic collaboration discovery
assertions: DM Realm is absent
dedicated resolver still returns it

semantic_cases.name: participant_authority_is_symmetric
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding active membership current authorization basis and active MLS generation are exact
semantic_cases.action: both participants create own messages
assertions: creator and peer use the same participant evaluator
technical root is not an operational owner

semantic_cases.name: third_participant_and_root_governance_denied
semantic_cases.precondition: stable Direct Conversation
semantic_cases.action: add third participant grant admin or modify peer message

semantic_cases.name: agent_reply_requires_conjunction
semantic_cases.precondition: Agent is a stable participant but runtime key or participation policy is not ready
semantic_cases.action: agent reply
assertions: resolver remains found or suspended independently

semantic_cases.name: list_next_prepare_input_authors_scope_update_and_tombstone
semantic_cases.precondition: one accepted non-terminal Contact round whose issuer-local lineage head is at version 1
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list and copy next_prepare_input into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update and of ak.self.contact.command.tombstone
assertions: the accepted row carries next_prepare_input and the three field names are byte-identical to the prepare fields that consume them
version equals current head version plus one and predecessor_event_ref equals the current lineage head Event ID, not the predecessor of that head
both prepare phases are accepted with the values copied verbatim and no client-side renaming, recomputation or derivation occurs
the same row is projected for a glare-derived basis, where predecessor_event_ref is the issuer's own request head
an empty granted_to_peer_scopes replacement keeps contact_state accepted and the row still carries the cursor so a later widen stays authorable

semantic_cases.name: non_authorable_contact_states_omit_next_prepare_input
semantic_cases.precondition: rows in pending_outgoing, pending_incoming, rejected, expired and tombstoned
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list
assertions: no row in these five states carries next_prepare_input, because the first two have no basis or lineage yet and the last three are terminal
the omission alone expresses that no successor is authorable now and no extra error code or contact_state value is introduced
a client MUST NOT assemble a successor from request_event_ref, response_event_ref or tombstone_event_ref

semantic_cases.name: glare_first_successor_uses_version_two
semantic_cases.precondition: a glare-derived accepted Contact round whose issuer-local lineage has only that issuer's request head and no versioned accepted successor
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list and prepare the first scope_update or tombstone successor with next_prepare_input copied verbatim
assertions: next_prepare_input.version is exactly 2
next_prepare_input.predecessor_event_ref is byte-identical to that issuer's own request Event ID
the request payload is not required to contain a lineage version and no synthetic version-1 ak.contact.accepted Event is created
every later successor uses current head version plus one and the exact current head Event ID

semantic_cases.name: glare_first_successor_rejects_wrong_bootstrap_edge
semantic_cases.precondition: the same glare-derived founding edge with no versioned accepted successor
semantic_cases.action: prepare the first successor with a version other than 2 or with a predecessor other than the issuer's own request Event ID
assertions: the server writes nothing
the verifier does not infer a missing request version and does not synthesize an accepted Event

semantic_cases.name: stale_next_prepare_input_is_refused_and_reread
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder holds a next_prepare_input read before a concurrent accepted successor advanced the lineage head
semantic_cases.action: prepare ak.self.contact.command.scope_update or ak.self.contact.command.tombstone with the stale triple
assertions: prepare is refused with zero writes and a scope replacement whose current proof is stale is refused with contact_scope_stale
the client re-reads ak.self.contact.read.list and retries with the fresh cursor
the client never guesses a lineage head and never retries the same triple

semantic_cases.name: sixteenth_generation_candidate_is_admitted
semantic_cases.precondition: fifteen not-yet-active candidate MLS groups already reference the same active-generation predecessor whole value
semantic_cases.action: submit the sixteenth ak.direct_conversation.mls_generation.activate candidate through ak.self.events.command.submit
assertions: the sixteenth candidate is admitted because the cap is sixteen and not fifteen
no candidate is activated by admission alone; the singleton cell still selects exactly one
the pair coordinates, binding, membership and current active generation are unchanged

semantic_cases.name: seventeenth_generation_candidate_is_refused_with_exact_code
semantic_cases.precondition: sixteen not-yet-active candidate MLS groups already reference the same active-generation predecessor whole value
semantic_cases.action: submit the seventeenth candidate through ak.self.events.command.submit and again through ak.peer.events.command.submit
assertions: both entry points refuse with that exact registered code at HTTP 409 and write nothing
the refusal is never reported as rate_limited and carries no retry_after_ms window, because activating or expiring an existing candidate is the only way forward
a generic failed_precondition or conflict is not an acceptable substitute once the code is registered

semantic_cases.name: generation_candidate_fanout_refusal_does_not_quarantine_the_pair
semantic_cases.precondition: the seventeenth candidate was just refused with mls_generation_proposal_fanout_exceeded
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair and send an ordinary Message on the current active generation
assertions: the pair is not quarantined and the resolver still returns the same coordinates, active_mls_generation_ref and active_mls_generation_value_digest
the resolver state does not become suspended and no send blocker is added for the refusal
the sixteen existing candidates are retained; the refusal removes none of them

semantic_cases.name: resolver_send_blockers_are_server_verifiable_only
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder blocked the peer in ak.account.blocklist and one historical epoch secret was never installed on this device
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair through ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve
assertions: found.send_blockers[] carries only blockers the service can prove from accepted authoritative state
personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are absent from the wire enum, so the service cannot report them even if it wanted to
the resolver state stays found; the client-local blockers do not turn it into suspended
the client merges its own client-local blockers on top of the wire set before deciding whether to release the send

semantic_cases.name: resolver_returning_a_client_local_blocker_is_schema_violation
semantic_cases.precondition: a service attempts to report a holder-private or device-private fact on the wire
semantic_cases.action: return found.send_blockers containing personal_blocked or history_key_unavailable
assertions: the closed direct_conversation_send_blocker enum no longer contains either value, so the reply fails schema validation at the client
the client MUST NOT accept the value by tolerating an unknown blocker string
no server-side evaluation of the holder blocklist or of device-local history key installation is protocol evidence

semantic_cases.name: presence_and_keypackage_blockers_are_participant_only
semantic_cases.precondition: the caller is not one of the two exact-pair participants of the requested pair
semantic_cases.action: probe ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve for that pair to learn peer presence or KeyPackage inventory
assertions: presence_offline and keypackage_empty are returned only to an existing exact-pair participant of that pair
a non-participant gets the same opaque failure as for a pair that does not exist, so the blockers cannot be used as an enumeration oracle
an existing pair is never hidden from a real participant merely because a peer is offline or has no KeyPackage inventory

semantic_cases.name: pending_incoming_row_authors_respond_and_reject
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder holds one verified mirror of a peer-authored ak.contact.requested plus the request_acceptance_receipt issued by the peer's own source service
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list and copy request_receipt into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.respond and of ak.self.contact.command.reject
assertions: the pending_incoming row carries the complete signed request_receipt object and the field name is byte-identical to the prepare field that consumes it
both prepare phases accept the receipt copied verbatim, with no narrowing to a reference and no change to the prepare contract
the receipt issuer is the peer's source service, not the holder's own server, so the client verifies the signature itself instead of trusting its server's retelling
the same receipt digest is the one that derives the normal basis, so respond and reject consume the identical bytes

semantic_cases.name: non_pending_incoming_states_omit_request_receipt
semantic_cases.precondition: rows in pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list
assertions: no row in these five states carries request_receipt, because pending_outgoing has no incoming request to answer and the other four have a consumed slot or a terminal round
the omission alone expresses that respond and reject are not authorable now; no error code and no contact_state value is added for it

a glare pair never presents a receipt-bearing row: an unconsumed outgoing request in the holder's own slot keeps the row pending_outgoing while glare evidence is still incomplete, and the mechanically derived basis projects accepted, so the row is never pending_incoming and respond and reject stay forbidden throughout

semantic_cases.name: contact_mirror_branch_returns_exact_event_without_seal
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder holds a Contact verified mirror whose receipt was cryptographically verified at ingest and CAS-stored, the contact row is pending_incoming, and the requester lives on a different Principal Server so the Event is absent from the holder's realm event store
semantic_cases.action: call ak.self.events.read.resolve for the exact request Event id with include_payload true
assertions: the exact signed Event and its complete payload are returned from the Contact verified mirror, so the client can recompute event_digest and check the receipt binding itself
the returned message field is the original plaintext rather than the delivery stub, because the stub rule constrains delivery surfaces and not the exact target holder
seals is empty and no covering Seal of the requester Principal Control Realm is disclosed through this branch
no Event other than the exact requested one is returned and no Realm membership is implied

semantic_cases.name: contact_mirror_branch_refuses_seal_refs_and_unverified_rows
semantic_cases.precondition: the same pending_incoming mirror, plus a second holder-local row that was stored without completing receipt verification at ingest
semantic_cases.action: call ak.self.events.read.resolve with seal_refs selecting the covering Seal, and separately for the Event backed only by the unverified local row
assertions: the seal_refs selector is never satisfied through the Contact mirror branch and is accounted into missing
the unverified local row does not open the branch, so a row stored without ingest-time receipt verification cannot be used as an independent authority
neither refusal reveals whether the underlying Event or Seal exists

semantic_cases.name: contact_mirror_visibility_closes_on_terminal_round
semantic_cases.precondition: the same mirror after the contact row transitions out of pending_incoming into accepted, rejected, expired or tombstoned
semantic_cases.action: call ak.self.events.read.resolve for the same exact request Event id
assertions: the transition clears request_receipt and closes resolve visibility in the same transaction, so the credential and the visibility share one lifetime
the selector is accounted into missing and is indistinguishable from a non-existent Event, and MUST NOT be reported under unauthorized
retained mirror bytes stay available for local audit but are never exposed through this surface again
